 Louis Casiano Fox News

 close Video California sheriff’s deputy, jail officer placed on leave after 5-second exchange with ICE 
 The exchange happened shortly before ICE agents detained a man hiding in a public courtyard, authorities said. (Credit: Orange County Sheriff’s Department)
 NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!
 Two California sheriff's department employees have been placed on administrative leave pending an investigation after a five-second conversation with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers outside a county jail.
 The Orange County Sheriff's Department announced Friday that surveillance video captured the Oct. 31 exchange outside the Intake Release Center. 
 A deputy and a sheriff’s special officer (SSO) were seen leaving the facility, approaching an SUV and "appearing to have a five-second conversation" with ICE officers, the department said.
 Moments after the sheriff's deputy and security officer walked away, a second vehicle arrived.
 EXCLUSIVE: LA ICE DIRECTOR REVEALS OFFICERS FOLLOWED HOME, HARASSED AS POLICE FAIL TO HELP IN SANCTUARY CITY 
 The Orange County Sheriff's Department put a deputy and jail officer on leave pending an investigation after video footage showed them having a five-second exchange with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers moments before a man hiding in a public courtyard was detained. (Orange County Sheriff's Department) 
 The ICE officers exited both vehicles and entered a public courtyard outside the visitor's entrance.
 There, they detained a man who appeared to be hiding, according to the sheriff's department. Authorities did not release the man's name or why he was detained.
 NEW MAINE LAW LIMITS POLICE COOPERATION WITH FEDERAL IMMIGRATION OFFICIALS 
 The sheriff's department has opened an internal investigation into the incident, which raises questions regarding compliance with California's Values Act (SB 54), a state law that strictly limits how local law enforcement can assist federal immigration authorities.
 Orange County Sheriff Don Barnes said his agency takes public safety and state compliance seriously.
 MARYLAND SHERIFF TORCHES DEMOCRATS OVER LAW HE SAYS PUTS ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS FIRST 
 Video released by the Orange County Sheriff's Department shows a man being detained by immigration authorities outside a county jail on Oct. 31. (Orange County Sheriff's Department) 
 "I will fully cooperate with ICE to the extent the law allows to prevent serious criminal offenders from returning to the communities they have preyed upon," Barnes said in a statement. 
 "Personnel acting outside the law and Department policy will be held appropriately accountable.
 Video "We will enforce state and local laws equally, without bias, and without concern for anyone’s citizenship," he added. "I want the community to continue to feel safe in calling for assistance, reporting crime and visiting the jail regardless of their immigration status."
 CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP 
 In a statement to Fox News Digital, a spokesperson for the Department of Homeland Security noted that seven of the 10 safest cities in the United States partner with ICE. 
 "Because some sanctuary states including California refuse to work with ICE law enforcement, criminal illegal aliens are released from jails into American communities to perpetuate more crimes," the statement said. "Partnerships with law enforcement are critical to having the resources we need to arrest criminal illegal aliens across the country."
 "Every day, DHS enforces the laws of the nation across the country, including in California," the statement added. 
 Local law enforcement worked with DHS, including helping to make 40,000 arrests in Florida and a two-week operation in West Virginia that resulted in the arrest of over 650 illegal aliens, the agency said.
